Propensity-score weights with the pieces needed to carry their estimation into the inference

Source: R/ps_weights.R
ps_weights.Rd

Fits (or takes) a logistic regression for a binary treatment and returns inverse-probability weights together with the influence of the fitted coefficients and the derivative of each weight in those coefficients. Passed as weight_model to df_counting(), KM_diff(), cumulative_rmst_bands() or plotKM.band_subgroups() with weight_variance = "estimated", the object lets standard errors, intervals, bands and tests account for the fact that the weights were estimated (see the section "Estimated weights" of df_counting()).

Usage

ps_weights(
  formula = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  type = c("ipw", "stabilized"),
  model = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'ps_weights'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

Arguments

formula

A formula for the treatment model, treatment (coded 0/1) on the left-hand side. Used with data; fitted by stats::glm(formula, family = stats::binomial(), data = data) with the default control, so that weights computed by hand from the same call agree.

data

Data frame holding the variables of formula: exactly the rows that will be analysed.

type

"ipw" (default): 1 / e for treated subjects and 1 / (1 - e) for controls, with e the fitted probability of treatment. "stabilized": those weights multiplied by the proportion treated (treated subjects) and the proportion not treated (controls).

model

An existing logistic glm fit, instead of formula and data. Give either formula and data, or model, not both.

x

A "ps_weights" object.

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class "ps_weights", a list with

weights

The weights, one per row.

type

"ipw" or "stabilized".

treat

The treatment (0/1), one per row.

ps

The fitted probabilities of treatment.

IF

Matrix, one row per subject and one column per estimated coefficient (aliased columns dropped): the influence of each subject on the coefficients.

dw

Matrix of the same shape: the derivative of each weight in the coefficients.

model

The glm fit.

call

The call.

print() shows the type, the number of rows and of coefficients, and by arm the size, the range of the weights and the effective sample size \((\sum w)^2 / \sum w^2\).

Details

With \(x_i\) the row of the model matrix of subject \(i\), \(A_i\) the treatment and \(e_i\) the fitted probability, $$IF_i = \Big\{\sum_j x_j x_j' e_j (1 - e_j)\Big\}^{-1} x_i (A_i - e_i)$$ is the influence of subject \(i\) on the fitted coefficients (the estimate minus its limit is approximately \(\sum_i IF_i\)), and the derivative of the weight of subject \(i\) in the coefficients is \(dw_i = -\{(1 - e_i) / e_i\} x_i\) for a treated subject and \(dw_i = \{e_i / (1 - e_i)\} x_i\) for a control. With type = "stabilized" the weights and dw are those of "ipw" multiplied by the arm proportion, which is treated as a fixed number; IF is the same.

The following are errors, each naming the problem: a model that is not a glm; a family other than binomial or a link other than logit; prior weights other than 1 or an offset; a fit that did not converge; a fitted probability within 1e-10 of 0 or 1; rows dropped for missing values; a response that does not take both values 0 and 1.

The weights are never truncated or rescaled. The rows of weights, treat, ps, IF and dw are in the order of the rows of the data the model was fitted on.

See also

df_counting() (section "Estimated weights"), KM_diff(), cox_rhogamma()

Other survival_analysis: KM_diff(), cox_rhogamma(), df_counting(), wt.rg.S()

Examples

library(survival)
gbsg$tte <- gbsg$rfstime / 30.4375
pw <- ps_weights(hormon ~ age + meno + size + grade + nodes + pgr + er, data = gbsg,
                 type = "stabilized")
pw
#> Propensity-score weights (stabilized): n = 686, 8 coefficients in the logistic model
#>        arm   n weight min weight max   ess ess / n
#>  treat = 1 246     0.4493       2.63 203.0  0.8253
#>  treat = 0 440     0.7379       1.85 417.7  0.9493
gbsg$sw <- pw$weights

# weights treated as known (the default) and with their estimation carried through
known <- KM_diff(gbsg, "tte", "status", "hormon", weight.name = "sw")
est <- KM_diff(gbsg, "tte", "status", "hormon", weight.name = "sw",
               weight_variance = "estimated", weight_model = pw)
identical(known$dhat, est$dhat)                       # estimates do not change
#> [1] TRUE
summary(sqrt(est$sig2_dhat / known$sig2_dhat))        # standard errors do
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.     NAs 
#>  0.9231  0.9330  0.9445  0.9468  0.9556  0.9979      14 

dc <- df_counting(gbsg, "tte", "status", "hormon", weight.name = "sw",
                  weight_variance = "estimated", weight_model = pw)
dc$ess                                                # effective sample size by arm
#>     group   n      ess     ratio
#> 1   treat 246 203.0308 0.8253283
#> 2 control 440 417.7090 0.9493386
cox_rhogamma(dc, scheme = "fh", scheme_params = list(rho = 0, gamma = 0))$hr_ci_asy
#>         beta  sig_bhat       hr     lower     upper
#> 1 -0.3747545 0.1276936 0.687458 0.5352457 0.8829562
